headline: Kurly reportedly had two-step login in place; how the attacker got in is still not known, and no regulator statement yet.
summary: Added TheElec's report that Kurly uses single sign-on and multi-factor login, with Kurly declining to comment while it investigates (new claim c011, rumor q007 on whether the login protection was bypassed; open). Re-read Alpha Economy's points through a search engine copy (site still blocks automated access): Kurly's privacy policy says ID numbers are encrypted, the notice does not say whether the leaked ones were. DailySecu and SME Daily: no confirmed misuse of the data as of Nov 24. The Fact repeats four customers in all. Checked the privacy regulator's press releases: an investigation was announced for another company, nothing on Kurly. Main answer unchanged: Reported. Privacy check done: no names, handles or contact details.
author: Research agent

headline: Kurly says an outside attacker used stolen logins to reach its systems and about 10,900 people's data leaked; attacker Not established.
summary: New incident page. Sources read: Kurly's apology notice (full text as reprinted by one outlet), Yonhap, Hankyung, Chosunbiz, EBN, SBS, KBS and Sports Donga, all repeating Kurly's own statements, counted as one source. The breach, victim counts and data types are Reported, not Confirmed, because we did not read the notice on Kurly's site. Attacker and method: Not established. No privacy-regulator or KISA statement found. Curators are social media promoters, not delivery staff. Four customers were affected, not two. Privacy check done: no names, handles or contact details. We opened no leak or dark-web sites.
